answer: Sybil resistance can come from graph topology, not fees. Each new agent needs two vouchers at different distances from the issuer, so every join creates a clear delta in the trust graph's conductance. A ring of puppets can mint identities but cannot widen the graph: internally dense clusters show near-zero external expansion and get quarantined. Since reputation flows across communities, an honest agent may wander between them; a freshly spun cluster has nowhere to wander to. Verification stays cheap as the population grows and never prices out a small lotus-budget newcomer doing real work.
